He said: "Whenever the boy passed by the monk, he would sit with him and listen to his words, and he was impressed by his speech. So whenever the boy came to the sorcerer, he would beat him and say: 'What delayed you?' And when he went to his family, he would sit with the monk listening to his words, and when he returned to his family, they would beat him and say: 'What delayed you?' So he complained of this to the monk, and the monk said to him: 'When the sorcerer says to you: "What delayed you?", say: "My family delayed me." And when your family says: "What delayed you?", say: "The sorcerer delayed me.'" Then while he was in that state, he passed along a road where there was a huge beast blocking the road, not letting people pass. The boy said: 'Now I will know: is the sorcerer's affair more pleasing to Allah, or the monk's affair?' He said: "So he took a stone," and he said: "O Allah, if the monk's affair is more beloved to You than the sorcerer's affair, then I throw this stone of mine so that it kills it and the people pass." He said: "So he threw it and killed it, and the people passed. The news of that reached the monk." He said: And the boy came to him, and the monk said to the boy: "You are better than I am, and if you are tested, do not point to me." He said: "The boy used to heal the blind from birth, the leper, and all other ailments. There was a companion of the king, and he went blind." He said: "It was said to him: 'There is a boy here who heals the blind from birth, the leper, and all other ailments; why do you not go to him?'" He said: "So he prepared gifts for him." He said: "Then he came to him and said: 'O boy, if you cure me, all these gifts are yours.' He said: 'I am not a physician who cures you, but Allah cures. If you believe, I will supplicate Allah to cure you.'" He said: "So the blind man believed, and he supplicated Allah, and He cured him. The one who had been blind then sat with the king as he used to sit. The king said to him: 'Were you not blind?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Who cured you?' He said: 'My Lord.' He said: 'And do you have a lord other than me?' He said: 'Yes, my Lord and your Lord is Allah.'" He said: "So [the king] seized him with punishment, and said: 'You will show me the one who taught you this.'" He said: "So he pointed to the boy, and [the king] summoned the boy and said: 'Turn back from your religion.'" He said: "But the boy refused." He said: "So [the king] seized him with punishment." He said: "So he pointed to the monk, and [the king] seized the monk and said: 'Turn back from your religion,' but he refused." He said: "So [the king] placed the saw on his head and split him until it reached the ground." He said: "Then he seized the blind man and said: 'You will certainly return, or I will certainly kill you.'" He said: "But the blind man refused, so [the king] placed the saw on his head and split him until it reached the ground. Then he said to the boy: 'You will certainly return, or I will certainly kill you.'" He said: "But [the boy] refused." He said: "Then [the king] said: 'Take him away and bring him to the summit of the mountain. If he turns back from his religion [well and good], otherwise throw him down.' So when they reached the summit of the mountain with him, they fell and all of them died. And the boy came walking until he entered upon the king, and [the king] said: 'Where are your companions?' He said: 'Allah has sufficed me against them.' He said: 'Take him away and carry him in a small boat, and take him into the middle of the sea. If he turns back from his religion [well and good], otherwise drown him.'" He said: "So they went with him, and when they had taken him into the middle of the sea, the boy said: 'O Allah, suffice me against them.' So the boat capsized with them." And the boy came walking until he entered upon the king, and the king said: "Where are your companions?" He said: "I supplicated Allah and He sufficed me against them." [The king] said: "I will certainly kill you." He said: "You will not kill me until you do what I command you." He said: "So the boy said to the king: 'Gather the people on one plain, then crucify me, then take an arrow from my quiver and shoot me, and say: "In the name of the Lord of the boy," for you will kill me thereby.'" He said: "So [the king] gathered the people on one plain." He said: "And he crucified him, and took an arrow from his quiver, placed it on the bowstring, then shot, saying: 'In the name of the Lord of the boy.' The arrow struck the boy's temple, so he placed his hand thus upon his temple, and the boy died. The people said: 'We believe in the Lord of the boy.' They said to the king: 'What you were fearing has happened; the people have believed.' So he commanded that the mouths of the lanes be seized, and [the trench] was dug and fires were kindled in it, and he seized them and said: 'If they turn back [well and good], otherwise throw them into the fire.'" He said: "So they threw them into the fire." He said: "Then a woman came with a child of hers." He said: "When she went to plunge in, she found the heat of the fire and drew back." He said: "Her child said to her: 'O mother, go on, for you are upon the truth,' and she plunged into the fire."

And others said: Rather, those who were burned by the fire were the disbelievers who tormented the believers.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ It was reported to me from 'Ammar, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: The people of the trench were a group of believers who had withdrawn from people during the interval (al-fitra, the period between prophets). A tyrant among the idol-worshippers sent to them, offered them to enter his religion, but they refused. So he dug a trench, kindled a fire in it, and gave them the choice between entering his religion or being thrown into the fire. They chose being thrown into the fire over returning from their religion, so they were thrown into the fire. Allah saved the believers who were thrown into the fire from the burning by seizing their souls before the fire touched them, and the fire came out to those on the edge of the trench of the disbelievers and burned them. That is the saying of Allah: ﴿For them is the punishment of Hell﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿and for them is the punishment of the Burning﴾ in this world.

It has been differed regarding the response (jawab al-qasam, the answer to the oath) to His saying ﴿By the sky containing the constellations﴾. Some of them said: its response is ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe.﴾

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: The oath occurs here: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe.﴾

And some of the grammarians of Basra said: The place of its oath, Allah knows best, is upon ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾; the lam was omitted, as He said: ﴿By the sun and its brightness... He has succeeded who purifies it﴾, meaning: "Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies it," so the lam was dropped. And if you wish, you may say it is by inversion, as if He said: "Destroyed were the people of the trench, and by the sky containing the constellations."

And some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is said in tafsir that the response of the oath in His saying ﴿Destroyed﴾ is like the oath of ﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾ in His saying ﴿He has succeeded﴾, this is in tafsir. They said: We have not found the Arabs omitting the oath without a lam that is followed by it, or "la" or "inna" or "ma." If that is so, then it is as if the response was left out, and then the place of the response was resumed with the statement, as is said in much speech: "Yā ayyuhā al-insān" (O mankind).

The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying of the one who said: the response of the oath in this is omitted, and the statement is resumed, because the Arabs do not drop the sign of the response of the oath from speech when they answer it.

And the more likely of the two interpretations of His saying ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾ is: The people of the trench were cursed, those who threw the believing men and women into the trench.

I only said that this is the more likely of the two interpretations for the reason we mentioned from al-Rabi', namely that Allah informed that for them is the punishment of the Burning along with the punishment of Hell. If they had not been burned in this world, the saying ﴿and for them is the punishment of the Burning﴾ would have no clear meaning alongside His informing that for them is the punishment of Hell, since the punishment of Hell is the punishment of the Burning together with all other kinds of its punishment in the Hereafter. And al-Ukhdud (the trench) is a pit dug in the earth.

* *

And regarding His saying ﴿the fire full of fuel﴾:

As for His saying ﴿al-nār﴾ (the fire): it is a repetition referring back to al-Ukhdud, and that is why it is in the genitive case (khafd). It is permissible to repeat it referring back to it while it is other than it, because it was in it; as if, since it was in it, it is it, so the speech proceeded upon it, for the addressees recognize it by its meaning. It is as if it was said: "Destroyed were the people of the fire full of fuel." By His saying ﴿dhāt al-wuqūd﴾ (full of fuel) He means: possessing abundant firewood. That is when the waw is vowelled with a fatḥa, al-waqūd (الوَقُود); as for al-wuqūd (الوُقُود) with a ḍamma, it means the blazing (al-ittiqād).

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 85, verses 1–5 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation (ta'wil, meaning the exegetical explanation) of the words of Allah, may His majesty be exalted and His names be sanctified: ﴿By the sky containing the constellations, and the promised Day, and the witness and the witnessed. Destroyed were the people of the trench, the fire fueled with fuel.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said, may Allah have mercy on him: As for His words, ﴿By the sky containing the constellations﴾, Allah, exalted is His praise, swore by the sky containing the constellations.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the meaning of "burudj" (constellations or towers) in this place. Some of them said: What is meant is "by the sky containing palaces," and they said: "burudj" means palaces.

Those who said this:
• Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿by the sky containing the constellations﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "Palaces in the sky." Someone else said: "Rather, they are the stars."
• I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿al-burudj﴾: "They claim they are palaces in the sky, and it is said they are the stars."

Others said: What is meant is "by the sky containing the stars," and they said: its stars are its "burudj."

Those who said this:
• Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the word of Allah ﴿containing the constellations﴾: "The burudj are the stars."
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, ﴿by the sky containing the constellations﴾: "The stars."
• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿by the sky containing the constellations﴾: "And its burudj: its stars."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is "by the sky containing sand and water."

Those who said this:
• al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah told me, saying: Husayn ibn Numayr told us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, regarding His words ﴿by the sky containing the constellations﴾: "Containing sand and water."

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is to say: the meaning is "by the sky containing the stations of the sun and the moon." This is because "burudj" is the plural of "burj" (tower, constellation), and they are stations which are constructed high above the earth and elevated. From this is the word of Allah: ﴿Even if you were within towers built high﴾ [4:78]. They are lofty, elevated stations in the sky, and there are twelve of them. The moon's course through each of them takes two and a third days, which totals twenty-eight stations, after which it is hidden for two nights. The sun's course through each of them takes a month.

* *

As for His words, ﴿and the promised Day﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: He swore by the Day which He promised His servants, for the decisive judgment between them, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

The exegetes said the same as what we have said about this, and a report has come from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Numayr and Ishaq al-Razi told us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The promised Day is the Day of Resurrection."
• He said: Waki' told us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the same.
• Ya'qub told us, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, saying: Yunus told us, saying: Ammar informed me, saying: Abu Hurayrah said: "The promised Day is the Day of Resurrection." Yunus said: And likewise al-Hasan said.
• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, ﴿and the promised Day﴾: meaning the Day of Resurrection.
• Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and the promised Day﴾: "The Resurrection."
• Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿the promised Day﴾: the Day of Resurrection.
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Yunus ibn Ubayd, from Ammar ibn Abi Ammar, client of the Banu Hashim, from Abu Hurayrah, ﴿and the promised Day﴾: the Day of Resurrection.
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The promised Day is the Day of Resurrection."
• Muhammad ibn Awf told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash told us, saying: My father told me, saying: Damdam ibn Zur'ah told me, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿The promised Day﴾ is the Day of Resurrection."

* *

As for His words, ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾:

The exegetes differed about the meaning of this. Some of them said: The meaning is: He swore by "the witness." They said: It is the day of Friday (Jumu'ah). And "the witnessed," they said, is the day of 'Arafah.

Those who said this:
• Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah informed us, saying: Yunus informed us, saying: Ammar informed me, saying: Abu Hurayrah said: "The witness is the day of Friday, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah." Yunus said: And likewise al-Hasan said.
• Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Harithah ibn Mudarrib narrate from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said regarding this verse ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: "The day of Friday and the day of 'Arafah."
• Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: He said: "The witness is the day of Friday, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah." It is also said: "The witness" is the human being, and "the witnessed" is the Day of Resurrection.
• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: "Two great days from the days of this world. We used to be told that the witness is the day of Friday and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: He said: "The witness is the day of Friday, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah."
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: He said: "The witness is the day of Friday, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah."
• Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿and the witness﴾ is the day of Friday, ﴿and the witnessed﴾ is the day of 'Arafah.
• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The witness: the day of Friday. The witnessed: the day of 'Arafah."
• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Numayr and Ishaq al-Razi told us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The witnessed is the day of 'Arafah, and the witness is the day of Friday."
• Sahl ibn Musa told us, saying: Ibn Abi Fudayk told us, from Ibn Harmalah, from Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the master of the days is the day of Friday, and it is the witness, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah."
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Musa ibn Ubayd, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The witnessed is the day of 'Arafah, and the witness is the day of Friday. In it there is an hour in which no believer coincides with it while calling upon Allah for good, except that He answers him, and he does not seek refuge with Him from evil, except that He protects him."
• Muhammad ibn Awf told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il told us, saying: My father told me, saying: Damdam ibn Zur'ah told me, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the witness is the day of Friday, and indeed the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah. So the day of Friday is Allah's choice for us."
• Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi told me, saying: Sufyan told us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmalah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "The master of the days is the day of Friday, and it is the witness."

Others said: The witness is Muhammad (ﷺ), and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection.

Those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Shu'bah, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf al-Makki, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The witness is Muhammad, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection." Then he recited: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day attended﴾ [11:103].
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mughirah, from Shabbak, who said: A man asked al-Hasan ibn Ali about ﴿the witness and the witnessed﴾. He said: "Have you asked anyone before me?" He said: "Yes, I asked Ibn Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr, and they said: the day of sacrifice and the day of Friday." He said: "No, but the witness is Muhammad." Then he recited: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ [4:41]. "And the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection." Then he recited: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day attended﴾.
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Abu al-Duha, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, who said: "The witness is Muhammad, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."
• Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' told me, saying: Sufyan told us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmalah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: ﴿and the witnessed﴾: the Day of Resurrection.

Others said: The witness is the human being, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection.

Those who said this:
• Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi told me, saying: Asbat told us, from Abd al-Malik, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: "The witness is the son of Adam, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."
• Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿the witness and the witnessed﴾: "The human being," and His words ﴿and the witnessed﴾: "The Day of Resurrection."
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: "The witness is the human being, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."
• Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: "The witness is the son of Adam, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."
• I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿the witness﴾: meaning the human being, ﴿and the witnessed﴾: the Day of Resurrection. Allah said: ﴿And that is a Day attended﴾.

Others said: The witness is Muhammad, and the witnessed is the day of Friday.

Those who said this:
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, from Yazid, from Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: "The witness is Muhammad, and the witnessed is the day of Friday." This is His saying: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾.

Others said: The witness is Allah, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection.

Those who said this:
• Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and the witness﴾: Allah says [it], and ﴿and the witnessed﴾: He says: the Day of Resurrection.

Others said: The witness is the day of sacrifice (Eid al-Adha), and the witnessed is the day of Friday.

Those who said this:
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mughirah, from Shabbak, who said: A man asked al-Hasan ibn Ali about ﴿the witness and the witnessed﴾. He said: "Have you asked anyone before me?" He said: "Yes, I asked Ibn Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr, and they said: the day of sacrifice and the day of Friday."

Others said: The witness is the day of sacrifice, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah.

Those who said this:
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: "The witness is the day of 'Arafah, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."

Others said: The witnessed is the day of Friday, and they narrated that from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The narration regarding that:
• Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: My uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb told me, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Zayd ibn Aymin, from Ubadah ibn Nusayy, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Increase your prayers upon me on the day of Friday, for it is a witnessed day, which the angels attend."

The correct statement regarding this, in our view, is to say: Indeed Allah swore by a witness who bears witness, and a witnessed [thing] that is witnessed. And He did not inform us, along with His oath, which witness and which witnessed He intended. All that we have mentioned, the scholars said: it is what is meant, as deserving to be called ﴿the witness and the witnessed﴾.

* *

As for His words, ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾:

He says: Cursed were the people of the trench. Some of them said: The meaning of His words ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾ is a report from Allah about the fire, that it destroyed them.

The scholars differed about the people of the trench: who were they? Some of them said: They were a people who had been People of the Book from among the remnants of the Magians (majus).

Those who said this:
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi told us, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza, who said: When the emigrants (muhajirun) returned from some of their campaigns, news of the death of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, reached them. Some of them said to others: "Which rulings apply to the Magians, since they are not People of the Book, nor are they among the polytheists of the Arabs?" Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "They were People of the Book, and wine had been made permissible for them. A king of theirs drank it until he became intoxicated, and he took his sister and had intercourse with her. When the intoxication left him, he said to her: 'Woe to you, what is the way out of what I have been afflicted with?' She said: 'Address the people and say: O people, indeed Allah has made marriage with sisters permissible.' So he stood up and addressed them, saying: 'O people, indeed Allah has made marriage with sisters permissible.' The people said: 'We disavow ourselves to Allah from this statement. No prophet brought it to us, and we did not find it in the Book of Allah.' So he returned to her, regretful, and said: 'Woe to you, indeed the people have refused me to acknowledge this.' She said: 'Lay the whips upon them.' He did so, and laid the whips upon them, but they refused to acknowledge it. He returned to her, regretful, and said: 'They have refused to acknowledge it.' She said: 'Address them, and if they refuse, then draw the sword against them.' He did so, but the people refused him. He said to her: 'The people have refused me.' She said: 'Dig a trench for them, then present to them the people of your kingdom. Whoever acknowledges, [spare him]; otherwise, throw him into the fire.' He did so. Then he presented to her the people of his kingdom, and whoever did not acknowledge he threw into the fire." So Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench, the fire fueled with fuel﴾ until ﴿except that they believe in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; and Allah is, over all things, Witness. Indeed, those who have tormented the believing men and believing women﴾, [who] burned them, ﴿and then did not repent, will have the punishment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the Burning﴾. And from that time they continued to permit marriage with sisters, daughters, and mothers.
• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾: He said: "We were told that Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: 'They were people in the irrigation channels of Yemen. Its believers and its disbelievers fought, and the believers prevailed over the disbelievers. Then they fought a second time, and the believers prevailed over the disbelievers. Then some of them took from others a covenant and binding pledges that none would betray another. But the disbelievers betrayed them and seized them completely. Then a man among the believers said to them: "Is there something good for you? Kindle a fire, then present us to it. Whoever follows you in your religion, that is what you desire. And whoever does not, leap into the fire, and you will be rid of him." So they kindled a fire and were presented to it. They began to throw their chieftains into it. Then there remained among them an old woman as if she hesitated, and a child in her lap said to her: "O mother, go on and do not waver." Allah has related to you their news and their account.'"
• Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾: He said: "It means the killers who killed them on the day they were killed."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench, the fire full of fuel﴾: He said: They were people from the Children of Israel who dug a trench in the earth, then kindled a fire in it, then stood men and women beside that trench, and they were exposed to it. They claimed that they were Daniel and his companions.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾: He said: There were cracks in the earth at Najran in which they used to torture people.

⁕ It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾: They claim that the people of the trench were from the Children of Israel. They seized men and women, dug a trench for them, then kindled fires in it, and stood the believers beside it, and said: "Either you disbelieve, or we will throw you into the fire."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to me, saying: Harami ibn 'Umara narrated to me, saying: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, saying: Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among those who were before you there was a king, and he had a sorcerer. The sorcerer said to the king: 'I have grown old, and my end has drawn near, so give me a boy to whom I may teach sorcery.'" He said: "So he gave him a boy to teach sorcery. The boy used to go to the sorcerer, and between the sorcerer and the king there was a monk." He said: "Whenever the boy passed by the monk, he would sit with him and listen to his words, and he was impressed by his speech. So whenever the boy came to the sorcerer, he would beat him and say: 'What delayed you?' And when he went to his family, he would sit with the monk listening to his words, and when he returned to his family, they would beat him and say: 'What delayed you?' So he complained of this to the monk, and the monk said to him: 'When the sorcerer says to you: "What delayed you?", say: "My family delayed me." And when your family says: "What delayed you?", say: "The sorcerer delayed me.'" Then while he was in that state, he passed along a road where there was a huge beast blocking the road, not letting people pass. The boy said: 'Now I will know: is the sorcerer's affair more pleasing to Allah, or the monk's affair?' He said: "So he took a stone," and he said: "O Allah, if the monk's affair is more beloved to You than the sorcerer's affair, then I throw this stone of mine so that it kills it and the people pass." He said: "So he threw it and killed it, and the people passed. The news of that reached the monk." He said: And the boy came to him, and the monk said to the boy: "You are better than I am, and if you are tested, do not point to me." He said: "The boy used to heal the blind from birth, the leper, and all other ailments. There was a companion of the king, and he went blind." He said: "It was said to him: 'There is a boy here who heals the blind from birth, the leper, and all other ailments; why do you not go to him?'" He said: "So he prepared gifts for him." He said: "Then he came to him and said: 'O boy, if you cure me, all these gifts are yours.' He said: 'I am not a physician who cures you, but Allah cures. If you believe, I will supplicate Allah to cure you.'" He said: "So the blind man believed, and he supplicated Allah, and He cured him. The one who had been blind then sat with the king as he used to sit. The king said to him: 'Were you not blind?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Who cured you?' He said: 'My Lord.' He said: 'And do you have a lord other than me?' He said: 'Yes, my Lord and your Lord is Allah.'" He said: "So [the king] seized him with punishment, and said: 'You will show me the one who taught you this.'" He said: "So he pointed to the boy, and [the king] summoned the boy and said: 'Turn back from your religion.'" He said: "But the boy refused." He said: "So [the king] seized him with punishment." He said: "So he pointed to the monk, and [the king] seized the monk and said: 'Turn back from your religion,' but he refused." He said: "So [the king] placed the saw on his head and split him until it reached the ground." He said: "Then he seized the blind man and said: 'You will certainly return, or I will certainly kill you.'" He said: "But the blind man refused, so [the king] placed the saw on his head and split him until it reached the ground. Then he said to the boy: 'You will certainly return, or I will certainly kill you.'" He said: "But [the boy] refused." He said: "Then [the king] said: 'Take him away and bring him to the summit of the mountain. If he turns back from his religion [well and good], otherwise throw him down.' So when they reached the summit of the mountain with him, they fell and all of them died. And the boy came walking until he entered upon the king, and [the king] said: 'Where are your companions?' He said: 'Allah has sufficed me against them.' He said: 'Take him away and carry him in a small boat, and take him into the middle of the sea. If he turns back from his religion [well and good], otherwise drown him.'" He said: "So they went with him, and when they had taken him into the middle of the sea, the boy said: 'O Allah, suffice me against them.' So the boat capsized with them." And the boy came walking until he entered upon the king, and the king said: "Where are your companions?" He said: "I supplicated Allah and He sufficed me against them." [The king] said: "I will certainly kill you." He said: "You will not kill me until you do what I command you." He said: "So the boy said to the king: 'Gather the people on one plain, then crucify me, then take an arrow from my quiver and shoot me, and say: "In the name of the Lord of the boy," for you will kill me thereby.'" He said: "So [the king] gathered the people on one plain." He said: "And he crucified him, and took an arrow from his quiver, placed it on the bowstring, then shot, saying: 'In the name of the Lord of the boy.' The arrow struck the boy's temple, so he placed his hand thus upon his temple, and the boy died. The people said: 'We believe in the Lord of the boy.' They said to the king: 'What you were fearing has happened; the people have believed.' So he commanded that the mouths of the lanes be seized, and [the trench] was dug and fires were kindled in it, and he seized them and said: 'If they turn back [well and good], otherwise throw them into the fire.'" He said: "So they threw them into the fire." He said: "Then a woman came with a child of hers." He said: "When she went to plunge in, she found the heat of the fire and drew back." He said: "Her child said to her: 'O mother, go on, for you are upon the truth,' and she plunged into the fire."

And others said: Rather, those who were burned by the fire were the disbelievers who tormented the believers.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ It was reported to me from 'Ammar, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: The people of the trench were a group of believers who had withdrawn from people during the interval (al-fitra, the period between prophets). A tyrant among the idol-worshippers sent to them, offered them to enter his religion, but they refused. So he dug a trench, kindled a fire in it, and gave them the choice between entering his religion or being thrown into the fire. They chose being thrown into the fire over returning from their religion, so they were thrown into the fire. Allah saved the believers who were thrown into the fire from the burning by seizing their souls before the fire touched them, and the fire came out to those on the edge of the trench of the disbelievers and burned them. That is the saying of Allah: ﴿For them is the punishment of Hell﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿and for them is the punishment of the Burning﴾ in this world.

It has been differed regarding the response (jawab al-qasam, the answer to the oath) to His saying ﴿By the sky containing the constellations﴾. Some of them said: its response is ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe.﴾

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: The oath occurs here: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe.﴾

And some of the grammarians of Basra said: The place of its oath, Allah knows best, is upon ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾; the lam was omitted, as He said: ﴿By the sun and its brightness... He has succeeded who purifies it﴾, meaning: "Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies it," so the lam was dropped. And if you wish, you may say it is by inversion, as if He said: "Destroyed were the people of the trench, and by the sky containing the constellations."

And some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is said in tafsir that the response of the oath in His saying ﴿Destroyed﴾ is like the oath of ﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾ in His saying ﴿He has succeeded﴾, this is in tafsir. They said: We have not found the Arabs omitting the oath without a lam that is followed by it, or "la" or "inna" or "ma." If that is so, then it is as if the response was left out, and then the place of the response was resumed with the statement, as is said in much speech: "Yā ayyuhā al-insān" (O mankind).

The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying of the one who said: the response of the oath in this is omitted, and the statement is resumed, because the Arabs do not drop the sign of the response of the oath from speech when they answer it.

And the more likely of the two interpretations of His saying ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾ is: The people of the trench were cursed, those who threw the believing men and women into the trench.

I only said that this is the more likely of the two interpretations for the reason we mentioned from al-Rabi', namely that Allah informed that for them is the punishment of the Burning along with the punishment of Hell. If they had not been burned in this world, the saying ﴿and for them is the punishment of the Burning﴾ would have no clear meaning alongside His informing that for them is the punishment of Hell, since the punishment of Hell is the punishment of the Burning together with all other kinds of its punishment in the Hereafter. And al-Ukhdud (the trench) is a pit dug in the earth.

* *

And regarding His saying ﴿the fire full of fuel﴾:

As for His saying ﴿al-nār﴾ (the fire): it is a repetition referring back to al-Ukhdud, and that is why it is in the genitive case (khafd). It is permissible to repeat it referring back to it while it is other than it, because it was in it; as if, since it was in it, it is it, so the speech proceeded upon it, for the addressees recognize it by its meaning. It is as if it was said: "Destroyed were the people of the fire full of fuel." By His saying ﴿dhāt al-wuqūd﴾ (full of fuel) He means: possessing abundant firewood. That is when the waw is vowelled with a fatḥa, al-waqūd (الوَقُود); as for al-wuqūd (الوُقُود) with a ḍamma, it means the blazing (al-ittiqād).

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 85, verses 1–5 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation (ta'wil, meaning the exegetical explanation) of the words of Allah, may His majesty be exalted and His names be sanctified: ﴿By the sky containing the constellations, and the promised Day, and the witness and the witnessed. Destroyed were the people of the trench, the fire fueled with fuel.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said, may Allah have mercy on him: As for His words, ﴿By the sky containing the constellations﴾, Allah, exalted is His praise, swore by the sky containing the constellations.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the meaning of "burudj" (constellations or towers) in this place. Some of them said: What is meant is "by the sky containing palaces," and they said: "burudj" means palaces.

Those who said this:
• Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿by the sky containing the constellations﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "Palaces in the sky." Someone else said: "Rather, they are the stars."
• I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿al-burudj﴾: "They claim they are palaces in the sky, and it is said they are the stars."

Others said: What is meant is "by the sky containing the stars," and they said: its stars are its "burudj."

Those who said this:
• Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the word of Allah ﴿containing the constellations﴾: "The burudj are the stars."
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, ﴿by the sky containing the constellations﴾: "The stars."
• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿by the sky containing the constellations﴾: "And its burudj: its stars."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is "by the sky containing sand and water."

Those who said this:
• al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah told me, saying: Husayn ibn Numayr told us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, regarding His words ﴿by the sky containing the constellations﴾: "Containing sand and water."

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is to say: the meaning is "by the sky containing the stations of the sun and the moon." This is because "burudj" is the plural of "burj" (tower, constellation), and they are stations which are constructed high above the earth and elevated. From this is the word of Allah: ﴿Even if you were within towers built high﴾ [4:78]. They are lofty, elevated stations in the sky, and there are twelve of them. The moon's course through each of them takes two and a third days, which totals twenty-eight stations, after which it is hidden for two nights. The sun's course through each of them takes a month.

* *

As for His words, ﴿and the promised Day﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: He swore by the Day which He promised His servants, for the decisive judgment between them, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

The exegetes said the same as what we have said about this, and a report has come from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Numayr and Ishaq al-Razi told us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The promised Day is the Day of Resurrection."
• He said: Waki' told us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the same.
• Ya'qub told us, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, saying: Yunus told us, saying: Ammar informed me, saying: Abu Hurayrah said: "The promised Day is the Day of Resurrection." Yunus said: And likewise al-Hasan said.
• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, ﴿and the promised Day﴾: meaning the Day of Resurrection.
• Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and the promised Day﴾: "The Resurrection."
• Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿the promised Day﴾: the Day of Resurrection.
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Yunus ibn Ubayd, from Ammar ibn Abi Ammar, client of the Banu Hashim, from Abu Hurayrah, ﴿and the promised Day﴾: the Day of Resurrection.
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The promised Day is the Day of Resurrection."
• Muhammad ibn Awf told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash told us, saying: My father told me, saying: Damdam ibn Zur'ah told me, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿The promised Day﴾ is the Day of Resurrection."

* *

As for His words, ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾:

The exegetes differed about the meaning of this. Some of them said: The meaning is: He swore by "the witness." They said: It is the day of Friday (Jumu'ah). And "the witnessed," they said, is the day of 'Arafah.

Those who said this:
• Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah informed us, saying: Yunus informed us, saying: Ammar informed me, saying: Abu Hurayrah said: "The witness is the day of Friday, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah." Yunus said: And likewise al-Hasan said.
• Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Harithah ibn Mudarrib narrate from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said regarding this verse ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: "The day of Friday and the day of 'Arafah."
• Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: He said: "The witness is the day of Friday, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah." It is also said: "The witness" is the human being, and "the witnessed" is the Day of Resurrection.
• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: "Two great days from the days of this world. We used to be told that the witness is the day of Friday and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: He said: "The witness is the day of Friday, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah."
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: He said: "The witness is the day of Friday, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah."
• Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿and the witness﴾ is the day of Friday, ﴿and the witnessed﴾ is the day of 'Arafah.
• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The witness: the day of Friday. The witnessed: the day of 'Arafah."
• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Numayr and Ishaq al-Razi told us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The witnessed is the day of 'Arafah, and the witness is the day of Friday."
• Sahl ibn Musa told us, saying: Ibn Abi Fudayk told us, from Ibn Harmalah, from Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the master of the days is the day of Friday, and it is the witness, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah."
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Musa ibn Ubayd, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The witnessed is the day of 'Arafah, and the witness is the day of Friday. In it there is an hour in which no believer coincides with it while calling upon Allah for good, except that He answers him, and he does not seek refuge with Him from evil, except that He protects him."
• Muhammad ibn Awf told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il told us, saying: My father told me, saying: Damdam ibn Zur'ah told me, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the witness is the day of Friday, and indeed the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah. So the day of Friday is Allah's choice for us."
• Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi told me, saying: Sufyan told us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmalah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "The master of the days is the day of Friday, and it is the witness."

Others said: The witness is Muhammad (ﷺ), and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection.

Those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Shu'bah, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf al-Makki, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The witness is Muhammad, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection." Then he recited: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day attended﴾ [11:103].
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mughirah, from Shabbak, who said: A man asked al-Hasan ibn Ali about ﴿the witness and the witnessed﴾. He said: "Have you asked anyone before me?" He said: "Yes, I asked Ibn Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr, and they said: the day of sacrifice and the day of Friday." He said: "No, but the witness is Muhammad." Then he recited: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ [4:41]. "And the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection." Then he recited: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day attended﴾.
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Abu al-Duha, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, who said: "The witness is Muhammad, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."
• Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' told me, saying: Sufyan told us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmalah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: ﴿and the witnessed﴾: the Day of Resurrection.

Others said: The witness is the human being, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection.

Those who said this:
• Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi told me, saying: Asbat told us, from Abd al-Malik, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: "The witness is the son of Adam, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."
• Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿the witness and the witnessed﴾: "The human being," and His words ﴿and the witnessed﴾: "The Day of Resurrection."
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: "The witness is the human being, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."
• Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: "The witness is the son of Adam, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."
• I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿the witness﴾: meaning the human being, ﴿and the witnessed﴾: the Day of Resurrection. Allah said: ﴿And that is a Day attended﴾.

Others said: The witness is Muhammad, and the witnessed is the day of Friday.

Those who said this:
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, from Yazid, from Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: "The witness is Muhammad, and the witnessed is the day of Friday." This is His saying: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾.

Others said: The witness is Allah, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection.

Those who said this:
• Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and the witness﴾: Allah says [it], and ﴿and the witnessed﴾: He says: the Day of Resurrection.

Others said: The witness is the day of sacrifice (Eid al-Adha), and the witnessed is the day of Friday.

Those who said this:
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mughirah, from Shabbak, who said: A man asked al-Hasan ibn Ali about ﴿the witness and the witnessed﴾. He said: "Have you asked anyone before me?" He said: "Yes, I asked Ibn Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr, and they said: the day of sacrifice and the day of Friday."

Others said: The witness is the day of sacrifice, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah.

Those who said this:
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and the witness and the witnessed﴾: "The witness is the day of 'Arafah, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."

Others said: The witnessed is the day of Friday, and they narrated that from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The narration regarding that:
• Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: My uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb told me, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Zayd ibn Aymin, from Ubadah ibn Nusayy, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Increase your prayers upon me on the day of Friday, for it is a witnessed day, which the angels attend."

The correct statement regarding this, in our view, is to say: Indeed Allah swore by a witness who bears witness, and a witnessed [thing] that is witnessed. And He did not inform us, along with His oath, which witness and which witnessed He intended. All that we have mentioned, the scholars said: it is what is meant, as deserving to be called ﴿the witness and the witnessed﴾.

* *

As for His words, ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾:

He says: Cursed were the people of the trench. Some of them said: The meaning of His words ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾ is a report from Allah about the fire, that it destroyed them.

The scholars differed about the people of the trench: who were they? Some of them said: They were a people who had been People of the Book from among the remnants of the Magians (majus).

Those who said this:
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi told us, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza, who said: When the emigrants (muhajirun) returned from some of their campaigns, news of the death of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, reached them. Some of them said to others: "Which rulings apply to the Magians, since they are not People of the Book, nor are they among the polytheists of the Arabs?" Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "They were People of the Book, and wine had been made permissible for them. A king of theirs drank it until he became intoxicated, and he took his sister and had intercourse with her. When the intoxication left him, he said to her: 'Woe to you, what is the way out of what I have been afflicted with?' She said: 'Address the people and say: O people, indeed Allah has made marriage with sisters permissible.' So he stood up and addressed them, saying: 'O people, indeed Allah has made marriage with sisters permissible.' The people said: 'We disavow ourselves to Allah from this statement. No prophet brought it to us, and we did not find it in the Book of Allah.' So he returned to her, regretful, and said: 'Woe to you, indeed the people have refused me to acknowledge this.' She said: 'Lay the whips upon them.' He did so, and laid the whips upon them, but they refused to acknowledge it. He returned to her, regretful, and said: 'They have refused to acknowledge it.' She said: 'Address them, and if they refuse, then draw the sword against them.' He did so, but the people refused him. He said to her: 'The people have refused me.' She said: 'Dig a trench for them, then present to them the people of your kingdom. Whoever acknowledges, [spare him]; otherwise, throw him into the fire.' He did so. Then he presented to her the people of his kingdom, and whoever did not acknowledge he threw into the fire." He said: "Then he seized the blind man and said: 'You will certainly return, or I will certainly kill you.'" He said: "But the blind man refused, so [the king] placed the saw on his head and split him until it reached the ground. It has been differed regarding the response (jawab al-qasam, the answer to the oath) to His saying ﴿By the sky containing the constellations﴾. Some of them said: its response is ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe.﴾

Mention of those who said this:

And if you wish, you may say it is by inversion, as if He said: "Destroyed were the people of the trench, and by the sky containing the constellations."

And some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is said in tafsir that the response of the oath in His saying ﴿Destroyed﴾ is like the oath of ﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾ in His saying ﴿He has succeeded﴾, this is in tafsir. They said: We have not found the Arabs omitting the oath without a lam that is followed by it, or "la" or "inna" or "ma." If that is so, then it is as if the response was left out, and then the place of the response was resumed with the statement, as is said in much speech: "Yā ayyuhā al-insān" (O mankind).

The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying of the one who said: the response of the oath in this is omitted, and the statement is resumed, because the Arabs do not drop the sign of the response of the oath from speech when they answer it.

And the more likely of the two interpretations of His saying ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾ is: The people of the trench were cursed, those who threw the believing men and women into the trench.

I only said that this is the more likely of the two interpretations for the reason we mentioned from al-Rabi', namely that Allah informed that for them is the punishment of the Burning along with the punishment of Hell. If they had not been burned in this world, the saying ﴿and for them is the punishment of the Burning﴾ would have no clear meaning alongside His informing that for them is the punishment of Hell, since the punishment of Hell is the punishment of the Burning together with all other kinds of its punishment in the Hereafter. And al-Ukhdud (the trench) is a pit dug in the earth.

And regarding His saying ﴿the fire full of fuel﴾:

As for His saying ﴿al-nār﴾ (the fire): it is a repetition referring back to al-Ukhdud, and that is why it is in the genitive case (khafd). It is permissible to repeat it referring back to it while it is other than it, because it was in it; as if, since it was in it, it is it, so the speech proceeded upon it, for the addressees recognize it by its meaning. It is as if it was said: "Destroyed were the people of the fire full of fuel." By His saying ﴿dhāt al-wuqūd﴾ (full of fuel) He means: possessing abundant firewood. That is when the waw is vowelled with a fatḥa, al-waqūd (الوَقُود); as for al-wuqūd (الوُقُود) with a ḍamma, it means the blazing (al-ittiqād).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 85, verses 6–8:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿When they were sitting over it, (6) And they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers. (7) And they did not resent them except because they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy. (8)﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "The fire, the fire full of fuel, when these disbelievers of the People of the Ditch were sitting over it", meaning over the fire. He said "over it" (ʿalayhā), and the meaning is that they were sitting on the edge of the ditch, but it was said "over the fire" (ʿalā al-nār), while the meaning is "at the rim of the ditch" (li-shafīr al-akhdūd), because the listeners know its meaning.

Qatadah used to say concerning this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿The fire full of fuel, when they were sitting over it﴾, that he meant by this the believers. This interpretation which Qatadah gave is according to the view of those who said that the People of the Ditch who were killed were from among the people of faith.

We have already shown that the correct interpretation of this is other than this view which Qatadah, before him, took.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 85, verses 11–12:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds will have gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great attainment﴾ [11] ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe﴾ [12].

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed, those who affirmed the oneness of God, namely these people whom the companions of the trench burned and other people of monotheism, ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, meaning: and acted in obedience to God, complied with His command, and refrained from what He forbade them. ﴿For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, meaning: for them in the Hereafter, with God, are orchards beneath which flow rivers of wine, milk and honey. ﴿That is the great attainment﴾, meaning: this which is for these believers in the Hereafter is the great victory in what they sought and pursued through their faith in God in the world, and their deeds in accordance with what God commanded them to do therein and was pleased with from them.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Indeed, the seizure of your Lord, O Muhammad, against whomever He seizes among His creation, which is His retribution upon whomever He takes vengeance against, is severe.
